papers.title: Total chemical synthesis of curcumin and symmetrical diarylheptanoid analogues.
papers.abstractText: Curcuminoids possess widespread medicinal relevance. We report a scalable three-step total synthesis of curcumin via boron-mediated condensation with an overall yield of 74% and high isomeric purity.

papers.title: Metabolic engineering of Escherichia coli for the de novo biosynthesis of curcumin from tyrosine.
papers.abstractText: Plant polyphenol bioproduction provides sustainable alternatives to field cultivation. By co-expressing phenylalanine ammonia-lyase and diketide-CoA synthase, recombinant E. coli produced 560 mg/L curcumin directly from amino acids.

papers.title: Supercritical fluid extraction of high-purity curcumin from Curcuma longa rhizomes.
papers.abstractText: Conventional solvent reflux can degrade heat-sensitive curcuminoids. Curcumin was selectively extracted using supercritical CO2 with ethanol co-solvent, yielding 8.2% w/w pure curcuminoid crystals.

papers.title: Enzymatic synthesis of curcuminoids using recombinant polyketide synthases.
papers.abstractText: Polyketide synthases govern natural diarylheptanoid diversity. Curcumin synthase 1 purified from turmeric catalyzed the in vitro condensation of feruloyl-diketide to yield authentic curcumin.

papers.title: Deep eutectic solvent-assisted extraction of curcumin from turmeric waste.
papers.abstractText: Circular valorization of spice processing residues requires non-toxic solvents. A choline chloride-lactic acid deep eutectic solvent extracted 94.5% of available curcumin from agro-industrial turmeric pomace under microwave irradiation.

papers.title: Heterologous production of curcumin in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
papers.abstractText: Yeast represents an ideal eukaryotic host for secondary metabolite cascades. Engineered yeast strains harboring the artificial curcuminoid pathway successfully synthesized curcumin from caffeic acid in batch fermentation.

papers.title: Microwave-promoted condensation for the rapid synthesis of curcumin.
papers.abstractText: Green chemistry emphasizes reaction atom economy and energy conservation. Curcumin was synthesized in 15 minutes by microwave irradiation of acetylacetone and vanillin in the presence of tributyl borate with an isolated yield of 81%.

papers.title: Aqueous two-phase extraction of curcumin using ionic liquid systems.
papers.abstractText: Aqueous biphasic partitioning enables simultaneous isolation and purification. The partition coefficient favored the top ionic phase, allowing 96.2% extraction of curcumin from crude Curcuma paste without organic evaporation steps.

papers.title: Semi-continuous extraction of natural curcumin using pressurized hot water.
papers.abstractText: Pressurized water extraction exploits reduced water polarity at elevated temperatures. Subcritical water at 140 °C produced an extract rich in curcumin without causing thermal decomposition.

papers.title: Chemoenzymatic cascade for asymmetric curcumin derivative synthesis.
papers.abstractText: Selective functionalization of polyphenol ketones is synthetically challenging. We demonstrated the production of curcumin and unsymmetrical curcuminoids using coupled lipase-peroxidase cascades.

papers.title: Curcumin was administered orally to mice at 50 mg/kg and reduced paw edema.
papers.abstractText: Evaluation of in vivo anti-inflammatory efficacy was performed in rodents. Curcumin was administered orally to mice at 50 mg/kg and reduced carrageenan-induced paw edema significantly over 6 hours without ulcerogenic side effects.
